picks.editorial_note: A Nature-published result showing AI can design novel physics experiments that outperform human-designed setups is a genuine breakthrough in AI-accelerated scientific discovery, not just an application of AI to an existing workflow.
picks.title: Artificial Intelligence Suggests New Physics Experiments

picks.editorial_note: Training LLMs to express calibrated uncertainty when proposing experiments tackles a core reliability problem in AI-driven science, with direct implications for how much autonomy researchers can safely hand to AI in the lab.
picks.title: An AI capable of doubt can optimize scientific discovery

picks.editorial_note: A $1.2M NSF grant spanning USF, Purdue, and UT Dallas to build quantum-resistant, AI-enabled security into next-generation wireless networks addresses a looming infrastructure vulnerability as quantum computing matures.
picks.title: USF faculty secure $1.2M NSF grant to advance quantum-secure, AI-enabled wireless networks

picks.editorial_note: An NSF-funded hybrid neuromorphic-quantum computing system that exploits thermal noise could meaningfully cut the energy footprint of AI computation, a pressing constraint as AI workloads scale.
picks.title: Grant funds hybrid system that could spur vast energy improvements to computing

picks.editorial_note: A nationwide German permit for RWTH Aachen's Level 4 autonomous research vehicle, built on an open-source driving stack, marks a concrete regulatory milestone for real-world autonomous vehicle deployment in Europe.
picks.title: RWTH Receives Nationwide Testing Permit for Autonomous Research Vehicle “karl.” | RWTH Aachen University | EN

picks.editorial_note: Federal cancellation of AHRQ healthcare research grants, including a Johns Hopkins AI project meant to speed lung cancer diagnosis, illustrates how policy shifts can directly stall promising AI-for-health work.
picks.title: Funding cuts hit research focused on making American healthcare safer, more efficient

picks.editorial_note: A high-profile Helmholtz viewpoint arguing Europe must build its own open frontier AI models reflects a strategic policy debate over AI sovereignty that is increasingly shaping national and EU research funding priorities.
picks.title: Why we in Germany and Europe need to build our own open frontier models

picks.editorial_note: Two major awards, including an Army Research Office grant for bio-inspired sensing hardware on unmanned systems, reflect sustained defense-sector investment in AI-enabled hardware research at UMass Amherst.
picks.title: ECE’s Qiangfei Xia and Colleagues Receive Two Awards for Trailblazing Research : Riccio College of Engineering : UMass Amherst

picks.editorial_note: UAB's Spiromatics startup translating years of academic research into a commercial AI diagnostic for lung disease is a concrete example of university AI research reaching patients through industry partnership.
picks.title: UAB startup brings decades of research to the future of lung care

picks.editorial_note: Princeton's finding that AI models misread key details in roughly 1 in 4 police bodycam analyses is a consequential accuracy gap given growing law-enforcement reliance on AI video analysis, with real policy stakes.
picks.title: AI tools can miss the mark on police bodycam footage
